The mandatory beneficial-owner declaration is filed with the registrar (greffe) of the commercial court, which maintains the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and ongoing screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions Lists, OFAC SDN List (where contractually required or for USD-clearing), and the French national asset-freeze list maintained by the Minister of Economy. PEP detection is compulsory under 4AMLD/5AMLD for all shareholders, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners. KYC/AML files must contain evidence of source of funds/wealth, corporate ownership chart, and sanctions/PEP screening reports. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and aviation-sector third-party intermediaries. TRACFIN reporting obligations arise under Article L.561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name and RCS availability checks performed via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr; final legal registry entry maintained by the greffe du tribunal de commerce (commercial court registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All filings are in French pursuant to Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 on the use of the French language. The SAS corporate name must be written using Latin script in the articles of association; non-Latin alphabets require an official French/Latin transliteration. The name must not be misleading, cannot imply an activity not actually carried out, and must be distinguishable from existing registered names and prior trademarks registered in France.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no statutory name pre-reservation registry for SAS; registration occurs through the Guichet unique upon incorporation. If the registrar refuses a name because it is confusing, prohibited, or requires ministerial authorization, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal. Procedure: 1) Rectify the proposed name or remove the prohibited token and resubmit the same draft through the Guichet unique within 15 days. 2) If the refusal relates to a regulated term requiring ministerial prior approval, obtain approval from the relevant authority (ACPR, AMF, ANAC or competent prefecture) and attach it to the rectified filing. 3) If the registrar maintains the refusal without legal grounds, the applicant may bring an appeal before the president of the competent tribunal judiciaire or tribunal de commerce, as applicable, under the supervisory jurisdiction of commercial registration matters within fifteen days from notification, submitting the refusal decision, the requested SIREN/name, and legal arguments. 4) Alternatively, a hierarchical administrative review may be addressed to the INPI Director for informal reconsideration. 5) The name cannot be used on commercial documents until the refusal is fully lifted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual/domiciliation office is legally acceptable for the registered seat of a French SAS under Articles L.123-11-2 and L.123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code, provided the company subscribes to a licensed domiciliation company service and the domiciliation contract is recorded in the RCS filing. However, for a commercial aircraft rotables and avionics surplus distribution business, the virtual office is only acceptable during the initial incorporation and first operational quarter; it does not satisfy commercial substance requirements for DGAC/FAA/EASA distribution oversight or French customs VAT registration. The company must establish a physically staffed and addressable office, warehouse, or contracted logistics facility in France before invoicing aircraft parts in the EU and must be able to demonstrate dedicated management, inventory control, and trade documentation presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% in the first 18 months after registration and 45% over three years, given the medium-risk enhanced aviation spares classification, cross-border payment rails via Escrow_Aviation and SWIFT Wire, and reliance on license-backed distribution of certified surplus parts. Physical inspection probability increases materially if any UBO is a politically exposed person, if the company transacts with high-risk jurisdictions, or if tax authorities observe a mismatch between reported substance and claimed operational presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-35 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) and Article L. 123-1 et seq. in respect of commercial registration; French Civil Code provisions applicable to legal persons.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, operating through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de Constitution d'une Société par Actions Simplifiée – Immatriculation au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (CERFA M0 / SD form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SAS (may be €1); however, for this cross-border aviation spares distribution activity a paid-up capital of at least €10,000 is recommended. The full subscribed capital must be deposited in a blocked bank or notarial escrow account before filing and released only upon issuance of the RCS certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned shareholder, constituting the sole member of the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) 'SurPlus Aviation SAS', hereby resolves: First, the share subscription to the initial paid-in capital of ten thousand euros is approved in full. Second, the registered office of the company is fixed at the address recorded in the statutory documents, deemed suitable for administrative, commercial, and aviation spares holding purposes, and shall be ratified. Third, the shareholder appoints as Président and sole officer the individual identified in the articles, with the widest powers to represent the company. Fourth, the executive is authorized to complete all registration, licensing, banking, and aviation-authority filings. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, notarization and signature of the articles of association (statuts) and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the department of the registered office, or an authorized commercial bank for the blocked capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language SAS articles of association reflecting the statutory requirements for an SAS. Have each shareholder execute the articles in person or by proxy. Open a temporary blocked account at a licensed bank or escrow account at the notary for the paid-up capital. Pay the funds immediately and obtain the certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds / certificat du notaire). The notary shall verify the identity and capacity of the signatories and the legality of the corporate purpose in respect of distribution of certified aircraft parts.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association (statuts) in French
Power of attorney for any proxy signatory
Certificate of paid-up capital deposit (attestation de blocage/consignation des fonds)
Identity documents (passport or national ID) of the shareholder and proposed legal representative
Draft capital attestation and bank receipt for the blocked funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a deficiency, complete the missing annexes or corrections within five business days and re-execute the instrument. If the selected bank refuses the account opening, select another licensed bank or complete the deposit through the notary's escrow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice of formation (Avis de constitution) in the legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (approved legal gazette) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the legal announcement containing the corporate form (SAS), company name, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and legal representative. Submit the announcement text to the approved gazette through its online or written order portal, pay the publication fee, and receive the attestation of publication required for the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Legal announcement draft
Company identification details (name, form, capital, registered office)
Declaration of corporate purpose and duration
Identity and powers of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette requests modification of the announcement, re-file the correct version promptly. In case of typographical errors, arrange a corrective publication within eight calendar days and attach it to the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the incorporation file with the commercial registry through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete statutory incorporation file online on the official Guichet Unique platform. Attach the signed articles, proof of legal announcement, blocked capital certificate, identity documents, powers of attorney, and the M0/SD declaration. Pay the required registry fees online. Upon successful review, the registry issues the RCS certificate (extrait K-bis) which constitutes full legal personality and commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Completed CERFA M0/SD declaration for incorporation
Two original or certified copies of the articles of association
Proof of publication of the legal notice (attestation de parution)
Bank or notarial certificate of paid-up capital
Identity/nationality documents of all legal representatives
Certificate of non-conviction (bulletin n°3 equivalent) where required
Justification of the registered office address (lease/ownership or accommodation letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries any document, submit the complementary response through the Guichet Unique within fifteen calendar days. If the filing is rejected, re-file the corrected dossier and, if necessary, request an order from the President of the Commercial Court to compel registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social and economic registration of the company (effectiveness of the taxpayer and employer status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF, and the local business regulation units
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the K-bis extract, register the company with the tax authorities for corporate income tax, VAT, and the self-employed business tax (formation professionnelle). Open the employer and payroll registrations with URSSAF if employees are engaged. Obtain the SIRET code and complete the administrative formalities with the commercial statistics bodies.
required_dossiers: RCS K-bis extract
Articles of association
Electronically signed tax and social declarations (formularies)
Identity and residence documents of legal representatives
Bank account details (RIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or URSSAF registration is delayed or the tax classification is disputed, contact the local tax office in writing and demand a formal classification notice. Administrative remedies and challenges may be filed within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the DGAC/EASA aviation parts supplier approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC) – Direction de la Sécurité de l'Aviation Civile (DSAC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to DGAC/DSAC the application for a French/EASA parts supplier certificate covering the distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus. Provide the conformity documentation required by EASA airworthiness regulations, including a quality system (EN/AS9120 or equivalent), traceability procedures, EASA Form 1 / FAA 8130-3 release control, storage and identification of serviceable parts, and a declaration of compliance with EU Regulation 2018/1139. Undergo the planned on-site audit and correct all findings prior to certificate issuance.
required_dossiers: Application form for aviation parts supplier approval
DGAC/EASA compliance manual for parts distribution
Scope of activities and list of aircraft part categories
EN/AS9120 or AS9110 quality management certificate (or implementation declaration)
Traceability and certificate-of-airworthiness documentation (EASA Form 1 / FAA 8130-3)
Storage, quarantine and release control procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If audit findings are raised, submit the corrective action plan to the DSAC within fourteen days. If the certificate is refused after audit and re-audit, file an administrative appeal within two months and, if necessary, petition the administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, environmental, occupational and civil defense clearance for the warehousing operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DRIEET (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement), Préfecture, and municipal fire safety authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the warehousing site qualifies as an ICPE registration or exemption. File the environmental and operational declaration with the DRIEET/Préfecture if the site stores hydraulic fluids, batteries, or hazardous components. Obtain the occupational safety inspection of the facility, arrange a structural load inspection for the aeronautical spare parts shelving and loads, and secure the municipal fire safety certification. Contract with an approved waste carrier for any decommissioned or non-airworthy material.
required_dossiers: ICPE registration or exemption declaration
Building occupancy certificate or lease authorization
Structural load inspection report for moving and storage areas
Fire safety inspection certificate
Waste segregation and disposal contracts with approved authorized carriers
Occupational health and safety risk assessment (DUERP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Préfecture or DRIEET asks for complementary information, provide a complete written response within the stated period. In case of refusal or objection, exercise the right of administrative appeal before the administrative court and simultaneously institute an amicable process before the public authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC) / Direction de la Sécurité de l'Aviation Civile (DSAC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'Agrément de Fournisseur de Pièces Aéronautiques (Aviation Parts Supplier Approval Certificate under EASA Part 21 / Part 145 compliance)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DRIEET – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (Regional Directorate for the Environment, Development and Housing) and the Préfet; administrative technical assistance from the Mission Régionale d'Autorité Environnementale (MRAe)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / simplified EIA (ICPE regime): not a full environmental impact assessment unless the storage site crosses Annex thresholds for hazardous waste treatment, in which case a full EIA study is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the French Environmental Code Articles R. 512-46 et seq. No free discharge of hydraulic fluids, fuels, batteries, or metal residues in industrial waste; VOC emissions remain below the 10 t/yr annual threshold set by Directive 1999/13/EC; wastewater discharge only under a prior authorization or connection to a compliant municipal network; waste traceability must be maintained through the French waste tracking system (BDES).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required for the storage facility, covering electrical installations, escape routes, extinguishing systems, and emergency signposting; structural load inspection verifying floor loading capacity appropriate to aircraft parts shelving; workplace clearance issued following an occupational health inspection and the production of the DUERP (document unique d'évaluation des risques professionnels).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the Central Bank and balance-of-payments statistical authority, with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for foreign-exchange legislative policy and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking and e-money supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area member; the euro is freely convertible with unrestricted capital and current-account transactions pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF). No exchange-control authorization or monetary compensation obligation applies. Profit remittance: qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders benefit from the 0% Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption; non-EU shareholders rely on treaty rates (typically 0-30%) or a 25% default withholding, subject to formalities such as the attestation de résidence fiscale and pre-payment return (RFI). Practical hurdles are limited to anti-money-laundering onboarding, tax-residency certification, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and balance-of-payments statistical declarations to the Banque de France for cross-border flows involving non-residents
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, compulsory conversion, or repatriation timeline exists under French external-finance regulations. Export receivables and foreign-currency accounts may be retained offshore or converted freely. A statistical reporting obligation applies where current-account and financial flows with non-residents individually exceed EUR 50,000 or aggregate monthly flows surpass the Banque de France threshold. Aircraft-parts export transactions remain subject to EU dual-use export-control screening and French customs clearance (EORI, DAU/formal entry), but not to FX surrender or conversion ratios

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and multicurrency Operational Account
EUR/USD Operational Account with trade-finance and documentary-collection line

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Aviation-escrow fiduciary account and Import/Export LC settlement account
Operational and FX forward settlement account
Multicurrency Operational Account for international wire settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Operational feasibility: Medium-High for euro-denominated expense payments through ACPR-licensed electronic-money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Treezor, Lydia Payments, Nickel); Low-Critical for aviation-escrow, commercial LC, and trade-finance rails because EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot legally take repayable deposits, issue letters of credit under UCP600, or provide escrow guarantees without breaching the French banking monopoly (CMF arts. L511-1 and L521-3). Offshore digital EMIs (UK-FCA, Lithuanian, or Cypriot authorized) have limited or no EU-passport access to France post-Brexit and lack the correspondent clearing and title-custody infrastructure required for aircraft-parts settlement; they may serve only as ancillary disbursement vehicles, never as the main treasury counterparty. A Tier-1 bank remains mandatory for the capital-blocking certificate and aviation escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed SAS with a non-resident or foreign legal representative, the ACPR-compliant KYC normally requires physical attendance of the Président at a French branch or a notarized face-to-face officer interview at an ACPR-recognized foreign branch. Remote onboarding is permitted only by bank discretion under ACPR Position 2019-09 using eIDAS-compliant electronic identification/video KYC, but is rarely extended to an aviation-parts trading entity in view of Medium-Risk-Enhanced classification. Where remote identity verification is refused, a French notaire may attest the passport and corporate documentation, and the legal representative must appear in person or grant a procuration notariée to a managing director resident in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or legal representative is domiciled in or connected to a high-risk jurisdiction, asset-protection trust, or FATF-listed territory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart certified by a French notary; audited parent accounts; credible-source statement for incorporation funded by a prior surplus-aircraft transaction; tax-residency certificates from the residence jurisdictions; Dun & Bradstreet or Bureau van Dijk compliance report; sworn declaration of no sanctions/tax-fraud exposure; supporting acquisition agreement and registration trail for the original aircraft asset.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Triangulation: payments to finance the purchase of surplus aircraft parts originate from non-resident third parties whose identity differs from the contractual counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master spares supply agreement with full conduit and beneficiary clauses; proforma invoice matched to the EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3 airworthiness certificate; customs entry (DAU) and EORI certificate; signed AWB/bl of lading; sanctions-screening screenshots timestamped before each payment; board resolution describing commercial rationale; confirmation that no broker or intermediary lacks an ASL/FAA-part-seller registration where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value escrow release requested prior to contractual custody period or without a coexisting ownership transfer document, raising invoice fraud/money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tri-party escrow agreement governed by French or English law with irrevocable release conditions; seller's legal title chain from deregistered fleet records; serial-number and airframe-hour trace documents; market valuation comparables for the specific rotable or avionics unit; accountant's comfort letter on cash-flow purpose; identity of the ultimate beneficial owners and confirmation of no same-day round-tripping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Routing of payments through OFAC, EU, or UK sanctioned countries, or any match (name, vessel, IP address, geolocation) against restrictive-measures lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening output retained in the bank-required format; EU dual-use classification decision (non-Annex-I) or export licence where applicable; end-user/end-use certificate signed by the buyer; contractual nexus confirming buyer is a certified civil-aircraft operator or MRO and not a state-linked military entity; compliance attestation by an in-house compliance officer and segregation of any military-grade technical data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared ISIC 4659 wholesale/parts-distribution scope and actual funding, including intermediary commission layers in jurisdictions with banking secrecy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Exact ISIC/NAICS mapping memo to the bank's industry code; statutory auditor's confirmation that inventory and receivables correspond to physical aircraft parts; list of sub-agents with full AML/KYC extraterritorial files; invoices at arm's-length margins; anti-bribery/anti-corruption compliance manual; annual financial projections demonstrating the business model as a staple stockist and not a shell financing arm.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a cash injection into FR_SAS (SAS in formation), funds must be deposited in a French bank blocked account or with a notary before registration; the bank issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds, and the funds are released only upon RCS registration. Inbound wire: SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 CT with beneficiary field naming the 'SAS in formation', reference line carrying 'Dépôt de capital social', and Purpose Code 'EQUI' (Equity Investment) under ISO 20022 external purpose codes; for an intra-group shareholder loan use 'INGO'. The Banque de France requires disclosure of the transaction's purpose for balance-of-payments statistics where thresholds are met; standard evidentiary pack: deed of subscription, shareholder board resolution, deposit certificate, and the EORI/registration slip.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of certified surplus-aircraft-parts purchases, the permitted rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV for non-documentary wire settlement with two-approver corporate banking authority; (2) Commercial letters of credit governed by ICC UCP600 with presentation of AWB, commercial invoice, EASA Form 1 (or FAA 8130-3), and inspection certificate to a French confirming bank; (3) Standby LC or bank-demand guarantee for escrow release mechanisms; (4) Documentary collections (DP/DA) for lower-value parts; and (5) ACPR-licensed tri-party aviation escrow settlement where the bank acts as neutral agent, releasing lodged proceeds only against digital title-disposal evidence and seller sign-off. All payments are subject to OFAC/EU sanctions screening, banque de France statistical declarations where the counterparty is non-EU, and CCF (contrôle des changes) legacy formalities abolished for current commercial transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD vanilla FX forwards (transactional hedging of firm purchase/sale commitments; no exchange-control restriction)
EUR/USD FX swaps for short-term treasury liquidity management (principal exchange/bo dere)
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for long-term capital or acquisition funding, subject to EMIR clearing and margin rules if the bank relationship is within the EU clearing threshold
Vanilla and barrier FX options (puts/calls on EUR/USD) for premium-based protection of trade margins

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) only for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies, expressly excluding EUR/USD trades, and only with parent-company treasury approval where the underlying exposure is lawful

Exotic commodity-linked hedging not applicable; currency forwards may be traded with the settlement bank only under an approved ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA, unless embedded in the bank's trade-finance offering

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registry information confirmation and annual contribution payment (Confirmation annuelle des informations du Registre national des sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the company's registered seat / Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due during the calendar month containing the anniversary of the company's RCS registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay the annual registry contribution by the end of the anniversary month triggers a formal demand by the Greffe; continued non-payment may lead to administrative removal (radiation) from the RCS, termination of legal existence, and loss of limited liability protection for obligations arising after radiation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder approval and deposit of annual statutory accounts (comptes annuels) with annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (electronic deposit via Infogreffe / formalites-auto platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end for shareholder approval; within 1 month of approval for deposit; absolute latest deposit date is 7 months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing exposes the legal representative to a criminal fine up to EUR 9,000; the court may issue an injunction with daily coercive penalties (astreinte) and refer the directors to the public prosecutor; the company may lose certain tax and registration benefits until filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax result declaration (liasse fiscale, form 2065 with attachments) and payment of any balance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year end, by the second business day after 1 May; for other fiscal year-ends, within 4 months from the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge of the tax due plus monthly late interest at 0.20% (intérêt de retard); penalties increase to 40% for fraud; failure to file after formal notice also subjects directors to a EUR 150 penalty per omitted schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation declaration (déclaration annuelle de TVA, form CA12) where the simplified real regime applies; monthly/quarterly VAT returns are submitted in other regimes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar fiscal year, filed by the second business day after 30 April of the following year; for a non-calendar year, within the same annual reconciliation deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment subjects the company to a 5% penalty on the amount due, increased to 10% after 30 days; plus monthly late interest; VAT may not be deferred after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership reconfirmation (bénéficiaires effectifs) in the RCS annual confirmation process; new UBO declaration required on any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the same time as the registry information confirmation; within 30 days after any change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-declaration of a change within 30 days exposes the directors to a criminal fine up to EUR 30,000 and, if intentional, imprisonment risk; the Greffe may also refuse subsequent filings until the UBO is properly updated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed if the company exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the fiscal year-end: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excluding VAT) exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees during the fiscal year exceeding 50. In addition, a mandatory auditor may be required by court order or by the statutory articles where specific governance conditions exist.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC 2014-03, Plan Comptable Général) for individual statutory accounts. IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts of listed groups but not for individual SAS accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial owner (UBO) details must be filed at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change. During the annual RCS information confirmation, the SAS is required to verify and confirm the correctness of the stored UBO data; if no change has occurred, no separate UBO declaration is due and the existing record is deemed confirmed on payment of the annual contribution.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000–$15,000 per annum for a mid-size trading company

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may qualify for a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to ownership, turnover and paid-in-capital conditions. Qualifying innovation and research expenditure may benefit from the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible research expenditure in metropolitan France, subject to statutory limitations and documentation. Certain capital gains, participation income and qualifying intellectual-property income may receive separate exemptions or reduced effective taxation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. Utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million per year plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Unused losses may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits and election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal impots.gouv.fr or through EDI-TDFC. The return is filed with the applicable tax package, including forms 2058-A and 2058-B for tax adjustments and loss utilization and forms 2059 series for capital gains, provisions and balance-sheet analysis.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax installments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the electronic return and tax package are generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year, subject to the standard additional electronic-filing tolerance where applicable. For a non-calendar year-end, filing is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, with specific rules for 31 December year-ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, fiscal year dates, tax office and legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder must not replace the French SAS's legal identity with the shareholder's details. Report the French SAS as the taxpayer and identify foreign parent entities only where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss transferred from the tax package after French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include profits attributable to the French SAS and its French taxable activities. Do not exclude transactions with foreign affiliates merely because the counterparty is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at the applicable rate, after credits, installments and prior-year adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SAS remains subject to French corporate income tax on its worldwide corporate profit, subject to applicable treaty allocation rules and foreign tax credit provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit or loss to taxable profit through permanent and temporary additions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation limitations, withholding taxes, foreign taxes, related-party adjustments and other cross-border tax differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss utilization, carryforward and, where elected, carryback information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% annual utilization cap and document any change in activity or ownership that could restrict preservation of tax losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities and other qualifying assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose gains on aircraft parts inventories as ordinary trading income rather than capital gains unless the assets are qualifying fixed assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Movements in provisions, depreciation and tax-relevant timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support provisions for obsolescence, certification expiry, warranty exposure and inventory impairment with SKU-level evidence, historical realization data and commercial documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting balance-sheet and income-statement data used to reconcile the statutory accounts with the tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain consistent treatment of foreign-currency purchases, customs values, intercompany balances, consignment stock, escrow receipts and customer advances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on certain deductible expenses and payments to related parties or foreign jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review management fees, royalties, financing charges, commissions, insurance, procurement fees and other payments to foreign group companies for deductibility, beneficial ownership and withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Four corporate income tax installments based generally on prior-year or current-year liability, followed by a final balancing payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign ownership does not eliminate installment obligations. Forecast taxable income and adjust installments where legally permitted to avoid late-payment interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment generally bears interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to file or incomplete filing may also trigger assessment by the tax authority, loss of tax attributes, denial of deductions, audit penalties and separate penalties for omitted information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and annual withholding-tax reporting forms filed electronically through impots.gouv.fr or applicable EDI channels; payroll and certain withholding obligations use separate declarations and payment systems.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven or periodic, depending on the payment category; annual corporate return for corporate tax and periodic filings for withholding obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withholding tax on qualifying payments to non-residents is generally declared and paid within the statutory period applicable to the payment and recipient category, commonly through the relevant French withholding form and electronic payment process. Dividend distributions may require payment of withholding tax within the applicable statutory period following payment or allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on dividends, interest, distributions and certain similar investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the recipient, gross payment, domestic withholding rate, treaty or exemption basis, amount withheld and payment date. Retain treaty forms and tax-residence evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate of residence and treaty claim for dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain the foreign tax authority's residence certification before payment where relief at source is sought; verify beneficial ownership and any anti-abuse or minimum holding-period conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate of residence and treaty claim for interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the lender's residence, beneficial ownership, debt instrument, arm's-length rate and absence of a French permanent establishment to which the debt claim is effectively connected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate of residence and treaty claim for royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the intellectual-property right, gross royalty, payer, recipient, beneficial owner and applicable treaty article. Separate software, know-how, technical services and bundled support.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may result in recovery of the unpaid tax from the payer, late-payment interest, a 10% surcharge or higher penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct, and potential denial of treaty-at-source treatment. Incorrect certificates and sham treaty claims may create joint tax, interest and penalty exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. Exemptions may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, including qualifying ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions. A tax treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 5%, 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty and ownership percentage.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of residence from the recipient's tax authority using Form 5000-FR and attach the relevant dividend, interest or royalty annex. Confirm beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose anti-abuse requirements where applicable, French permanent-establishment status, minimum holding periods and any EU exemption conditions. Apply the reduced rate only where procedural evidence is complete; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue the statutory refund process. Maintain board resolutions, distribution records, payment evidence, ownership charts, tax-residence certificates and beneficial-owner representations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents may be subject to French domestic withholding, generally at 25%, subject to statutory classification, recipient status and treaty relief. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories and payments recharacterized under anti-abuse rules. Treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% or 15% and interest withholding to 0% to 15%. The treaty rate must be verified under the specific bilateral convention.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets, or ownership or control of an entity meeting the threshold, generally triggers the French full transfer-pricing documentation requirement under Article L13 AA of the French Tax Procedures Book. A simplified documentation requirement generally applies below that threshold for taxpayers subject to transfer-pricing scrutiny. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone regime identical to a separate offshore Economic Substance Regulations code. Substance is enforced through the general anti-abuse doctrine, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, permanent-establishment principles and transfer-pricing requirements. A French SAS distributing surplus commercial aircraft parts should maintain French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, inventory and logistics control, customer and supplier functions, risk management, bank activity, accounting records and evidence that the company performs the functions for which it earns its margin.
industry_specific_transfer_pricing_contr: Benchmark procurement, quality-control, certification, warranty, inventory-obsolescence, logistics, financing and customer-credit risks separately rather than applying an unsupported group-wide margin.

Document the commercial rationale and arm's-length pricing for intercompany aircraft-part purchases, resale transactions, technical support, software, certification data, warehousing, insurance, financing and management services.
Retain traceability from part number and certification status to purchase order, customs entry, inventory ledger, sale invoice, delivery record and warranty or return record.
Use customs valuation and transfer-pricing positions consistently where possible, while separately analyzing customs and direct-tax legal standards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, issuing false invoices, understating inventory or margin, fabricating aircraft-part traceability, diverting sales outside the books, or knowingly claiming unsupported deductions or tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of tax, late-payment interest, administrative surcharges generally ranging from 10% to 80%, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with aggravated cases potentially reaching seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, tax penalties and civil liability where they personally participated in, authorized or facilitated the conduct. Courts may impose management bans and confiscation. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from judicial control, arrest warrants or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring inventory, cash, receivables or aircraft-part stock to related parties below value, preferring insiders, destroying accounting records or continuing trading while knowingly unable to pay debts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Bankruptcy-related criminal offenses may result in imprisonment, fines, director-management bans and civil claims by the insolvency practitioner or creditors. Exact sanctions depend on the offense and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for insufficient assets, wrongful trading-type conduct, management misconduct, restitution and contribution claims. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced; personal liability requires a statutory basis or proven personal fault.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and hidden profit distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting profit through excessive royalties, procurement fees, financing charges, management fees, guarantees or underpriced exports to related parties without functions, assets and risks supporting the charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions, withholding-tax recovery, interest, penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct and possible documentation-related penalties. Significant penalties may apply for failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they knowingly organized fraudulent profit diversion or misused corporate assets. Ordinary unsuccessful pricing judgments do not alone create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying aircraft parts, undervaluing imports, falsifying origin, bypassing export controls, misdescribing military or dual-use items, or shipping parts without required authorization, end-user controls or records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, seizure, forfeiture, customs fines and criminal sanctions may apply. Export-control breaches may produce administrative restrictions, criminal penalties and denial of future authorizations, depending on the goods and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and officers may be prosecuted where they ordered, knowingly approved or negligently enabled unlawful shipments. Travel restrictions, asset freezes or imprisonment depend on judicial action and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, using opaque escrow structures, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions alerts, structuring transactions to avoid controls or dealing with sanctioned counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential criminal money-laundering penalties include imprisonment and fines, with aggravated treatment for habitual, organized or professional conduct. Separate sanctions may arise under financial-sanctions, customs and payment regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and employees may be individually liable for knowing participation, facilitation or deliberate failure to act. Corporate fines, confiscation, professional bans and judicial restrictions may accompany individual sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying aircraft parts, technical data or financing to embargoed destinations, designated persons, prohibited airlines or restricted end users, directly or through intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Asset freezes, payment blocking, administrative enforcement, customs seizure, substantial criminal fines and imprisonment may apply under applicable French and European Union sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who approve or facilitate prohibited transactions may face prosecution, asset restrictions, management bans and imprisonment. A compliance-policy failure alone is not equivalent to criminal intent, but deliberate blindness and serious negligence may be relevant.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate veil abuse and sham-company conduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a nominee vehicle, commingling personal and corporate funds, conducting no genuine business, fabricating substance, using straw directors or creating the company solely to defeat tax, customs or creditor claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible tax reassessment under abuse-of-law principles, nullification or disregard of transactions, insolvency claims, asset seizure, management bans and criminal fraud or money-laundering sanctions where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: French law does not automatically pierce the corporate veil. Personal liability may nevertheless arise from misuse of corporate assets, management fault, fraudulent concealment, guarantees, statutory insolvency claims or direct criminal participation. Travel bans and imprisonment require a specific judicial or criminal basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete books, failing to preserve invoices and customs records, submitting inaccurate annual accounts, omitting beneficial-owner information or obstructing a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, rejection of accounts, tax assessment, penalties for obstruction or missing information, and criminal sanctions for false accounts or related offenses may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and persons responsible for accounting may incur personal civil or criminal liability for knowingly false accounts, obstruction or deliberate record destruction. Sanctions may include management bans and restitution.
